title: Geometry and networks
summary: Polygon angles, congruent and similar figures, circle chords, angles and tangents, and networks: graphs, Euler circuits and shortest paths.

cards.title: Review of geometry
cards.rule: Interior angle sum of an \(n\)-gon: \((n - 2) \times 180^\circ\). Exterior angles add to 360°.

cards.title: Congruent triangles and quadrilaterals
cards.rule: Tests: SSS, SAS, AAS, RHS. Use them to prove properties of shapes.
lines: In a parallelogram, the diagonals cut it into congruent triangles (AAS), so the diagonals bisect each other

cards.title: Similar figures and triangles
cards.rule: Scale factor \(k\): lengths \(\times k\), areas \(\times k^2\), volumes \(\times k^3\).
lines: Similar triangles, matching sides 4 and 10: \(k = 2.5\), so side 6 matches \(15\)

cards.title: Circles and chords
cards.rule: A line from the centre at right angles to a chord bisects the chord.
lines: Chord 16, radius 10: distance from the centre \(\sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = 6\)
cards.note: Chord, arc, sector, segment, tangent, secant: know each word.

cards.title: Angle properties of circles
cards.rule: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Angles in the same segment are equal.
lines: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180° (110° opposite 70°)

cards.title: Circles and tangents
cards.rule: A tangent meets the radius at 90°. Two tangents from one point are equal.
cards.note: Alternate segment theorem: tangent–chord angle equals the angle in the opposite segment.

cards.title: Chords, secants and tangents
cards.rule: Chords: \(AP \times PB = CP \times PD\). Tangent: \(PT^2 = PA \times PB\).

cards.title: Introduction to networks
cards.rule: Vertices (dots) joined by edges. The degree of a vertex is the number of edges at it.
lines: The degrees always add to twice the number of edges

cards.title: Isomorphic and planar graphs
cards.rule: Isomorphic: same connections, drawn differently. Planar: can be drawn with no crossing edges.
lines: Euler's formula for planar graphs: \(v - e + f = 2\)

cards.title: Trails, paths and Euler circuits
cards.rule: Trail: no repeated edges. Path: no repeated vertices.
lines: Euler circuit: every vertex has an even degree
Euler trail: exactly two odd vertices (start at one, finish at the other)

cards.title: Shortest path problems
cards.rule: Add the weights along each route and keep the smallest at every vertex.
lines: A to B 4, B to D 3, A to C 2, C to D 6
A–B–D = 7, A–C–D = 8, so the shortest is **7**
